_comment: Published measurements used to turn computation (FLOPs) into energy until a hardware meter is used. Each anchor gives joules per GFLOP for a class of device. Values marked derived are computed in pipeline/s03c_energy.py from the cited figures; the derivation is printed in results.

low_cost_arm_board.label: low-cost ARM board (Raspberry Pi 4, 4 x Cortex-A72)
low_cost_arm_board.source: Gondi (2022), Wav2Vec2.0 on the Edge: Performance Evaluation, arXiv:2202.05993

reported.model: wav2vec 2.0 Base (95 M parameters), PyTorch, CPU

low_cost_arm_board.flops_reference: wav2vec 2.0 Base on 10 s of audio, counted with the same FLOP counter as this study (results/s03c/energy_anchors.json)
low_cost_arm_board.note: 11 mWh matches added power x inference time (2.9 W x RTF 1.36 x 10 s = 39 J), so it is the energy caused by the workload, idle excluded.

apple_laptop_cpu.label: Apple Silicon laptop CPU (M1 to M2, all performance cores)
apple_laptop_cpu.source: Notebookcheck (2022), Apple M2 SoC analysis: Cinebench R23 multi-core package power
apple_laptop_cpu.throughput_reference: XLSR-53 forward pass measured on the author's MacBook Pro, Apple Silicon cores, 4 threads (results/s03c/apple_throughput.json)
apple_laptop_cpu.note: Package power under an all-core benchmark is an upper-range figure for a 4-thread inference load; the resulting energy is a bracket, not a measurement.
